subject: Using stan functions in an R package

messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Using stan functions in an R package
parts:
Hi all - 

I have a few stan functions that I've exported to R using `expose_stan_functions`; these are being called from within R functions. I'd like to bottle my R functions up into a package, but I don't know the easiest way of including stan functions. 

Does anyone have experience doing this? One work-around would be to use the C++ code for the functions and then use this approach (http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/src.html). Is this the simplest approach? 

Cheers, 
Jim

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: Using stan functions in an R package
parts: Broadly yes, use expose_stan_functions, find the .cpp code it generates (it should be in your temp directory), and maybe massage that a little so that it can be compiled when your package is installed.  I haven't gone through this process in a while so I can't offer specific advice.  If you post problems you run into here I'm happy to follow up. Krzysztof

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Using stan functions in an R package
parts:
On Monday, September 21, 2015 at 8:54:24 AM UTC-4, Jonah wrote:
Yeah I think what Krzysztof is suggesting should be possible. Definitely let us know if you get it to work (that would be good to know) or run into trouble.

The expose_stan_functions() function ultimately calls Rcpp::sourceCpp(), so basically if you fish the .cpp file out of tempdir(), then you just need to follow the Rcpp vignettes for using Rcpp within a package rather than from R's global environment.

Ben
